description: Use this when the user wants a work breakdown structure (WBS) chart or a project breakdown drawn from an outline, for example "make a WBS chart of this project" or "turn this task list into a WBS with codes and cost totals". Takes the outline (indent per level, or codes such as 1.2.3 on each line) with optional hours=, cost= and owner= fields, a layout (top-down or left-right), a page size and a title. Returns codes, rolled-up hours and cost per item and for the project, problems such as a parent value that differs from its children, a geometry check, the PDF page count, an interactive chart, and PDF, SVG and CSV downloads. Refuses an outline that mixes styles or skips a level, naming the line. Up to 400 items and 8 levels. Does not schedule tasks or add dates. Download links of large charts expire after about 1 hour.

orientation.description: Chart layout: top-down (deliverables side by side with their work listed below) or left-right (one column per level). Leave it out to get the layout that needs fewer PDF pages (top-down on a tie). Example: top-down.

outline.description:
The work outline, one item per line, up to 40,000 characters and 400 items. Either indent 2 spaces (or 4, or 1 tab) per level, or start every line with a code such as "1.2.3 Name". Optional fields after the name, separated by "|": hours=40, cost=1,200.50 (at most 2 decimals, one currency symbol such as $ for the whole chart), owner=Ana. Example: "Website
  Design | hours=40 | cost=2,000
  Build
    Front end | hours=80 | owner=Ana".

page_size.description: PDF page: letter (default), a4 or tabloid (11 x 17 in).

style.description: How levels are written: auto (default; numbered when each line starts with a code such as 1 or 1.2, refused when only some lines do), indent (use it when item names start with a number, such as 3.5 inch drives), or numbered. Example: auto.

title.description: Chart title, printed on the chart and used in file names, up to 80 characters, e.g. "Website relaunch". When the outline has several top-level items, the title also names the project box above them.
